Former Legislative Council member Wong Kam-fai is charged with dangerous driving and other offences, and is currently on bail awaiting trial. He served as a councillor from December 2022 to July this year. According to a review of LegCo records by "集誌社" (Collective Citizen), the total operating expenses of his office during his over-42-month term exceeded HK$10 million, including more than HK$1.5 million in consultancy fees. He successively appointed Chan Tak-ming, president of the "Hong Kong Guangzhou Innovation and Technology Association" he founded, and vice-president Ng Hok-ling, as consultants. Chan Tak-ming had been continuously engaged since January 2023, receiving HK$20,000 to HK$30,000 per month, totalling more than HK$1 million in consultancy fees. According to the guidelines on Legislative Council members' application for reimbursement of operating expenses, "a member should not engage a political party or any organisation over which his/her political party has control as a consultant." Is there any problem with hiring key members of related organisations as paid consultants? The LegCo Secretariat replied to enquiries from "集誌社" stating that the guidelines have been set out and no further comments would be added. Wong Kam-fai, who has no political affiliations, responded by saying that the association is all voluntary work and operates on a non-profit basis. In addition, at the tail end of his first term, Wong Kam-fai also distributed bonuses to his office staff, with the total staff expenses declared to the LegCo for that month exceeding HK$773,000.

Office operating expenses during term exceed HK$10 million

"集誌社" reviewed Wong Kam-fai's "reimbursement amounts for office operating expenses" in the 7th Legislative Council, which ranged from approximately HK$2.877 million to HK$2.984 million annually; from October 2025 onwards, in the 8th Legislative Council, the amount has been increased to HK$3.02 million. During his 42 months in office, Wong Kam-fai declared office operating expenses exceeding HK$10 million to the LegCo. In 2023 and 2024, his declared expenses were approximately HK$1.846 million and HK$2.89 million respectively.

However, in 2025, Wong Kam-fai's declared expenses were HK$4.006 million. The increase in expenses was due to reasons including staff expenses rising from HK$2.24 million the previous year to HK$3.215 million; consultancy fees also increased from HK$480,000 to HK$640,000. After Wong Kam-fai was re-elected in 2026, his expenses from January to June were HK$1.413 million.

Spent over HK$1 million hiring senior executives of his own association as legislative consultants

According to records, from February 2023 to June 2026, Wong Kam-fai declared consultancy fees exceeding HK$1.5 million to the LegCo. During the 36 months from 2023 to 2025, he consistently engaged Chan Tak-ming, president of the "Hong Kong Guangzhou Innovation and Technology Association," as a consultant at HK$30,000 per month, spending HK$1.08 million. After his re-election in the current term until his resignation, over six months, he continued to engage Chan Tak-ming at HK$20,000 per month, spending a total of HK$120,000. The "Hong Kong Guangzhou Innovation and Technology Association" was founded by Wong Kam-fai in 2016, where he served as executive president.

Three consultancy tenders, two bidders were members of the "Association"

As early as March 2023, Wong Kam-fai submitted tender documents for declaration to the LegCo. At that time, the three consultancy tenders were from Dai Chengfeng, Chan Tak-ming, and Cheng Kwok-wai. Among them, both Dai and Chan were members of the "Hong Kong Guangzhou Innovation and Technology Association," with Dai serving as head of the finance team. Dai quoted HK$45,000, Cheng quoted HK$35,000, and Chan's quote was the lowest at HK$30,000; ultimately Chan secured the consultancy work.

The tender's scope of work indicated that Chan's consultancy work involved assisting in advocating and planning innovation and technology, education, various social policies and issues; assisting in maintaining interactive communication across sectors; and assisting in supporting the various work of the regional office.

Hiring association vice-president as consultant with only one quote

Wong Kam-fai also engaged association vice-president Ng Hok-ling as a consultant. From June 2023, Ng Hok-ling served as Wong Kam-fai's consultant on innovation and technology and education policy matters, receiving HK$5,000 in consultancy fees in the first month, followed by HK$10,000 per month, totalling HK$315,000. Ng Hok-ling's consultancy work had only one quote. Regarding the scope of work in the tender, Wong Kam-fai stated that Ng "is simultaneously well-versed in both innovation and technology and education policies," "can respond quickly to work requirements, offers flexible service forms, and the service quality meets the needs of my parliamentary work."

LegCo guidelines: Should not engage organisations under party control as consultants

According to Article 24 of the Legislative Council's "Guidelines on Application for Reimbursement of Operating Expenses by Members," "a member should not engage his/her political party or any company/organisation in which his/her political party has a financial interest or control as a consultant."

Wong Kam-fai, who has no political affiliations: Association operates on a non-profit basis

"集誌社" enquired with Wong Kam-fai whether hiring key members of related organisations as consultants might conflict with the guidelines. Wong Kam-fai replied that Chan Tak-ming's portfolio covered district and political liaison, while Ng Hok-ling handled education. Wong Kam-fai said the association was founded by a group of like-minded innovation and technology professionals hoping to contribute to Hong Kong and mainland China's innovation and technology development. "Everyone does voluntary work, and it has always operated on a non-profit basis."

Office director received HK$276,000 upon completion of contract

In addition to consultancy expenses, regarding the salary expenses of legislative assistants, according to records, upon completing his term in 2025, Wong Kam-fai declared two staff expense items to the LegCo totalling more than HK$773,000, of which approximately HK$423,000 covered paid leave, together with November and December salaries.

Wong Kam-fai also distributed approximately HK$350,000 in bonuses to five office staff. Among them, Wong Kam-fai's office director had a monthly salary of HK$63,500. Upon the completion of her term in December, she received paid annual leave compensation, together with two months' salary totalling approximately HK$181,000, plus a bonus equivalent to 1.5 months' salary of HK$95,200, totalling HK$276,000. The other four received bonuses from Wong Kam-fai equivalent to 2.5 months' salary, ranging from HK$54,000 to HK$75,000.

LegCo Secretariat: Guidelines for reimbursement of operating expenses have been set out

"集誌社" previously enquired with the LegCo Secretariat about the appropriateness of Wong Kam-fai's practices of engaging the president and vice-president of his affiliated association as long-term consultants and distributing bonuses. The Secretariat replied that the relevant details had been set out in the guidelines for Legislative Council members' application for reimbursement of operating expenses, and no further comments would be added.

According to the "Guidelines for Application for Reimbursement of Operating Expenses," members may set aside funds from the reimbursement amount for office operating expenses to pay for contract bonuses, double pay, or end-of-contract gratuities, among other items. The amount of reserved funds should be determined according to contracts signed by both parties and other legal liabilities, and should not be excessive; members may receive payment without having to submit supporting documents.

In the declaration records, Wong Kam-fai marked the bonus amount as "Other," stating that no bonuses had been issued in the three years prior to the term, representing a discretionary arrangement, "and therefore was not specified in the contract." He also said that the team had assisted in promoting and implementing various bills, motions, and initiatives, and that "after careful consideration of the office's financial situation, having decided to issue bonuses to the following staff members to reward them for their hard work and contributions during the 7th Legislative Council term."

On 29 June this year, Wong Kam-fai was suspected of hitting two vehicles within the Chinese University campus and fleeing the scene. He was arrested by police on suspicion of four offences including drink driving and careless driving. When the incident was exposed by the media on 1 July, Wong had not declared it to the LegCo, and had attended the Reunification Day reception as usual to take photos. It was not until 3 July that Wong Kam-fai resigned from all his positions in the Legislative Council.

Apart from being a member of the LegCo Election Committee constituency, Wong Kam-fai is also a member of the 14th National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, and Associate Dean (External Affairs) of the CUHK Faculty of Engineering. Following the drink driving incident, CUHK announced the suspension of his administrative duties, which remains in effect. In September this year, police formally charged him with four offences including "dangerous driving," and he was granted bail. The case has been adjourned until 11 November for mention.
